fullPassage: When Malawi was troubled with a famine, thousands of people starved and died. William's family also struggled financially and they were unable to pay the eighty-dollar-a-year tuition for William's education. He had to drop out of school. However, he did not stop holding his passion for technology and spent most of his time at the local library, where he discovered a book about windmills and renewable energy. Electricity and running water were luxuries that only two percent of Malawians could afford. William decided to build a windmill to generate electricity and started to collect scrap materials around his village. "People said I was crazy. They thought I was out of my mind. They crowded around me, curious about what I was making," said William. Even though many people in his community did not believe he could succeed, he eventually built a functioning windmill using old bicycle wheels, PVC pipes, and old tractor fan blades. His first windmill lit four light bulbs and the villagers lined up to charge their cell phones. He started making bigger windmills and provided enough power for lights at night. He also built a solar-powered water pump. This 'brought the rain' and helped the villagers fight against the drought and famine that came back every season. His achievement gained national and international attention, and he was invited to speak at various events and conferences to share his story and inspire others. He also received a full scholarship from Dartmouth College in the U.S. and completed environmental studies there. His story shows the power of creativity and determination, and is an inspiration for anyone who doubts the power of one individual's ability to change the community. William's story is just one example of the potential that exists in Africa. Despite facing numerous challenges like poverty, corruption, and political instability, Africa has seen a rapid growth in technology adoption, innovation, and entrepreneurship. With over 60% of Africans under the age of 25, the continent has a large pool of young individuals who are eager to innovate and create new businesses. From mobile money platforms to solar-powered irrigation systems, African innovators are finding new and innovative ways to address some of the continent's most pressing challenges, such as access to healthcare, education, and clean energy. Recently, mobile money platforms such as M-Pesa have emerged as a popular alternative to traditional banking. Mobile money has enabled millions of Africans to access financial services and has helped to drive economic growth and development. With abundant sunlight, companies like M-Kopa Solar brought affordable solar power to millions of households across the continent. E-commerce platforms such as Jumia and Konga are bringing the convenience of online shopping to African consumers, while agritech startups like FarmCrowdy are using technology to improve agricultural productivity and reduce food waste. Healthtech startups like mPharma are providing data analytics platform to make drugs more affordable for Africans. Overall, Africa's technological development is a promising sign for the continent's future. As more young people are educated and empowered to pursue careers in technology, and as governments and businesses invest in the continent's infrastructure and resources, Africa will continue to grow and thrive. With its rich cultural diversity, abundant natural resources, and thriving tech ecosystem, Africa is ready to play a vital role in technological innovation and progress in the years to come.
title: William Kamkwamba's Electric Wind & Remarkable Changes in Africa
